title: Shared Folder Access
description: Create a shared group and configure a project directory so two contractors can collaborate safely.
scenario: Two contractors, alice and bob, must collaborate on /srv/projectx. The directory is currently owned by root:root with 755 permissions, so neither of them can write to it. Files they will create must stay editable by both — which is exactly what a shared group plus the setgid bit is for. There is no projectx group yet.
symptoms: bob gets 'Permission denied' when saving files in /srv/projectx
alice can read but not write either
Files created by one of them are not editable by the other
No shared group for the project exists in /etc/group
mission: Create a projectx group, put alice and bob in it, change the group of /srv/projectx recursively to projectx, and set the directory permissions to 2770 (setgid + rwx for group, nothing for others).

hints.title: One group to rule them all
hints.content: Create the group first with `sudo groupadd projectx`, then add both users with `usermod -aG`.

hints.title: Group ownership
hints.content: `chgrp -R projectx /srv/projectx` changes the group of the directory and everything inside it.

hints.title: The setgid bit
hints.content: On a directory, chmod 2770 sets the setgid bit: every NEW file inside automatically inherits the directory's group, so alice and bob stay in the same group without manual chgrp.

hints.title: Verify like an admin
hints.content: `stat -c '%U %G %a' /srv/projectx` shows owner, group and numeric permissions in one line.

acceptance_criteria.description: both alice and bob are members of projectx
/srv/projectx permissions are 2770 (setgid, group rwx, no access for others)
